svg.text: Advisor Compact Report: Synthetic-Only 784x6 Review Count Sweep
Final reporting threshold: 0.5 | Synthetic-only, grouped by perfume_id | Advisor-response / supplementary analysis

This report gathers the completed 784x6 synthetic-only experiment. It answers whether increasing the number of synthetic reviews changes model performance when using only synthetic rows. It should not
be presented as the main thesis benchmark because there are no YouTube rows in this sweep.
Perfumes were shuffled first, then complete six-review perfume blocks were selected for each count. Threshold sensitivity was checked; threshold 0.5 is used here as the single reporting threshold.
Emotion-rich synthetic v2, 784 perfumes x 6 review-level rows
Existing Gemini 3.1 Pro browser-labeled synthetic v2 corpus
Separate add-on generated with the same v2 method; existing rows were not re-labeled
Same source identity/context keyword files, same seed 20260612, no emotion/VAD label conditioning
Gemini 3.1 Pro browser labels; model-generated reference labels, not human annotation
Synthetic-only analysis; no YouTube rows are mixed into training or evaluation
NRC, VAD, Hartmann, Savani, GoEmotions, Cardiff
0.5 for final reporting; sensitivity checked at 0.25, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7
Macro F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC; official targets exclude anger
7. Main Threshold-0.5 Metrics, Mean +/- SD Across 5 Random Perfume Orders
At threshold 0.5, Logistic Regression has its best mean Macro F1 at 2,004 reviews (0.5795), while 4,704 reviews is essentially tied (0.5787) and has the best ROC-AUC and PR-AUC. XGBoost has its best
mean Macro F1 at the full 4,704-review condition (0.5953).
Higher review counts have very small SD, so they are more stable across random perfume-order seeds. The curve is not perfectly monotonic, so the careful claim is stability and generally stronger
ranking metrics, not automatic F1 improvement at every added count.
Threshold 0.5 was selected after sensitivity checks. A finer LR-only check found 0.49 was marginally highest on the full corpus, but it was effectively tied with 0.5; 0.5 is cleaner for reporting.
ROC-AUC and PR-AUC do not change with threshold because they use ranking scores.
Recommended advisor wording: This is synthetic-only advisor-response evidence about the synthetic corpus, not the main thesis benchmark.
The 784x3 pilot and 784x6 reporting run are not a direct replacement comparison. The 784x6 corpus adds review indices 4-6 with additional labeled text diversity, and the final reporting threshold is
0.5 rather than 0.3. Lower F1 in 784x6 should be read as a harder and broader synthetic corpus, not as failed generation.
Status: committed outputs exist for labels, 784x6 combined features, threshold sensitivity, focused threshold-0.5 sweep, and advisor-facing report images.
